A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FDA research, with matching authors, method, and experimental framework. Text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval and visual-grounding experiments, adversarial evaluations, ablations, zero-shot results, and attention analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results, including the detailed benchmark and ablation tables in its appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the function-word masking, parallel attention calculations, gated subtraction, minimum operation, and concatenation in Equations 1–7. The dictionary correction removes a duplicated 'to'; its 91 unique words are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate retrieval on Flickr30k and MSCOCO and grounding on RefCOCO+, retaining targeted, untargeted, and zero-shot evaluations. The newly discussed LLaVA and Qwen models are not evaluated.

E2.justification: The FDA comparisons retain TeCoA, FARE, no defense, masking and de-attention variants, and SIM-N/SIM-δ/SIM-2δ. The adaptive-selection comparison moves from v1 Table 7 to v3 Appendix A, Table 10, without losing comparators.

E3.justification: The Section 4.3 summary changes its attack description from untargeted to targeted, while plug-and-play table captions change from 'targeted and untargeted' to untargeted only. These reported-setting corrections agree with the existing appendix descriptions; the PDFs do not establish reruns. Training budgets, perturbation bounds, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 removes the introductory function-versus-content similarity diagnostic and the noun-removal condition from the motivating comparison, while adding adjective- and verb-removal attention-map controls in Figure 1. The substantive masking, hyperparameter, adaptive-selection, zero-shot, and alignment analyses remain, including relocated material.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Figure 3's similarity-spread reporting and the adaptive-selection mean/standard-deviation thresholds are retained unchanged.

E6.justification: V3 Table 10 corrects misplaced columns in v1 Table 7: SIM-N now has 25.95% function words and clean R@1 values of 95.90/85.50. Other retained score tables are numerically unchanged. The introductory 80.3%-versus-0% similarity result disappears, and v1 Table 1's 0.54% function-word ASR reduction becomes 99.54% relative ASR in v3 Figure 1, implying a different 0.46% reduction.

T1.justification: The method equations, adaptive-selection thresholds, and mathematical evaluation definitions retain their substance. Neither version introduces theorems or proofs; v3's semantic-gap explanation is conceptual rather than a formal derivation.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains improving robustness through function-word de-attention while preserving clean performance. The abstracts retain the same experimental scope, headline ASR reductions, and scalability, generalization, and zero-shot claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds a semantic-gap explanation for attacks favoring function words and practical layer/head recommendations. Section 4.5 adds dictionary-optimality uncertainty and discusses untested LLaVA/Qwen applicability. Its claim of seamless adoption on projector-based models replaces the limitations paragraph's explicit CLIP incompatibility discussion, without new validation.

D1.justification: The abstract changes promised code release to stated availability, and a new reproducibility statement promises checkpoints and reproduction/transfer instructions. The dictionary description changes from 93 to 91 words and removes a duplicate entry. These are documentation corrections, not evidence of a different implemented dictionary.

R1.justification: V3 adds contextual citations on purification, adversarial detection, LLaVA/Qwen, LoRA, token pruning, and spatial reasoning. The substantive positioning around adversarial-training trade-offs and differential attention remains; publication updates to existing Tian papers do not constitute new cited research.

P1.justification: V3 rewrites the introductory motivation, revises the limitations and conclusion, reorders the ablation discussion, and moves adaptive selection into Appendix A. It also adds a takeaway and acknowledgment, ethics, and reproducibility statements. The main section sequence and most technical exposition remain.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column format to a largely single-column ICLR layout, extensively resizing and relocating tables, figures, and equations. Figure 1 combines a normalized bar chart with expanded attention-map controls; the adaptive-selection table moves to the appendix and corrects column assignments. Figure 4 moves to the final page.

improvement.justification: V3 provides a limited net improvement through the corrected adaptive-selection columns and dictionary documentation, additional visual controls, and clearer code-access information. These repairs improve interpretability without changing the main empirical evidence. The gains are tempered by removal of the introductory similarity diagnostic, a small ASR inconsistency in the revised Figure 1, and unvalidated claims about projector-based model applicability.
